title: Red Onion Chutney
subtitle: Jammy, sweet-sharp chutney, the essential cheese board preserve
excerpt: Red onion chutney is slow-cooked with balsamic vinegar, red wine vinegar, and brown sugar until thick and almost jam-like. It goes with everything on a cheese board. Makes about three 300 g jars.
sourceNotes: British cheese board preserve staple. Balsamic vinegar brings sweetness and body; red wine vinegar brings sharpness.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made at least 2 weeks ahead; the flavour improves markedly.

content.text: Red onion chutney is made by long, slow cooking of red onions with balsamic and red wine vinegar until the mixture becomes almost jam-like,  dark, glossy, and thick. It works alongside strong cheese, cold meats, and pâté. The longer it rests in the jar, the better it gets. Makes about three 300 g jars.

Heat the olive oil in a large, wide pan over low heat. Add the sliced onions and salt. Cook gently, stirring occasionally, for 20 to 25 minutes until the onions are completely soft and starting to turn jammy. Don't rush this stage,  the onions need to caramelise slowly, not fry.

Add the sugar, both vinegars, and the thyme. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring regularly, until the chutney is thick and glossy and the liquid has reduced to almost nothing. Remove the thyme sprigs.
Ladle into hot sterilised jars while hot. Seal immediately.

items.symptom: Onions are still crunchy after 20 minutes
items.cause: Heat was too high, they were frying, not sweating.
items.fix: Reduce the heat, add a splash of water, and continue cooking until completely soft. Onions must break down fully before the vinegar goes in.

items.cause: Too much red wine vinegar relative to balsamic.
items.fix: Increase the balsamic component or reduce red wine vinegar to 60 ml. Balsamic adds sweetness alongside acidity.

items.cause: Reducing too hard in the last stage.
items.fix: Keep the heat at a gentle simmer in the last 15 minutes and stir constantly.

items.symptom: Thin texture even after 35 minutes of reduction
items.cause: The onions released more water than expected.
items.fix: Continue cooking, the chutney will always thicken further on cooling. The final texture should look slightly too thin when hot.

content.text: Sealed: 12 months in a cool dark place. Refrigerate once opened and use within 4 weeks.
